**The complete ITER ensemble now passes the declared numerical convergence
checks.** [all 33 original cases reach five seconds at all three maximum-step settings: 99 of 99 valid trajectories and 264 of 264 passing endpoint comparisons]{.claim}[C-305](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-305){.cid .st-measured}. This resolves the tested baseline's convergence
blocker for the current model and settings. The [primer](../primer.qmd) explains
the coupled simulation and its guarded surrogates.

We reran the original design using the
[strict physical-residual solve and continuous transport closure](97-strict-physical-residuals-and-continuous-transport.qmd).
Every original case and member remains in the design. The transition widths and
radial coefficient smoothing stay fixed across this comparison. The completed
sentinels were re-audited alongside the remaining fresh trajectories.

Each case has three adaptive maximum-step settings. Both adjacent comparisons
must pass for fusion power, stored thermal energy, and axis electron and ion
temperature. A finer-cap result supplies each relative-error denominator.
[the largest changes are 0.219% for coarse-to-middle and 0.0423% for middle-to-fine, both below the 1% acceptance limit]{.claim}[C-306](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-306){.cid .st-measured}. No case is discarded to obtain the pass.

The final audit reconstructs the equations from raw cell storage, transport and
source terms, checks every accepted step, and binds all reporting endpoints to
raw profiles and quantities. [maximum accepted physical-channel L1 is 1.76 × 10^−9^ against a 10^−8^ gate, and native mean L1 is 1.01 × 10^−14^ against 10^−10^; no crash occurs]{.claim}[C-307](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-307){.cid .st-measured}. It also retains the failed
proposals rather than hiding them: [372,141 accepted proposals and 2,659 rejected proposals are retained in 23,100 raw chunks; rejected-step rollback and retry schedules pass reconstruction]{.claim}[C-308](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-308){.cid .st-measured}.

The audit is separate from the integration's acceptance decision. Source and
input hashes, scheduler completion and both adjacent comparisons are required
for the combined pass. Successful process exit alone never supplies convergence.

This is a substantial change from the earlier unresolved numerical baseline.
It is also a precisely scoped result: the successful continuous closure differs
from the earlier hard-switch closure. These adaptive-cap comparisons establish
neither a fixed-step convergence order nor experimental physical validity.
Smoothing-width robustness and a direct particle-flux formulation remain separate
studies. The historical uncertainty results have not been silently recomputed.

M5's numerical baseline passes; physicist sign-off remains pending. The next
uncertainty study must explicitly use this baseline and its complete declared
design.
